problems.title: Which heap?
problems.statement: Keeping the k largest elements of a stream.

parts.prompt: After the stream, the top is…

problems.solution: The top of a size-k min-heap is the weakest survivor: the one to evict, and at the end the k-th largest.

problems.title: Trace

parts.prompt: Heap size after processing the 4th element?

problems.solution: The three largest are 9, 9, 7, so the answer is 7 (duplicates count).

problems.title: Costs

parts.prompt: Size-k heap: n · log₂ k operations, in millions (log₂ 10 ≈ 3.3)?
Full sort: n · log₂ n, in millions (log₂ 10⁶ ≈ 20)?

problems.solution: About 3.3M versus 20M, and the heap version works on a stream with O(k) memory.

problems.title: Top-k frequent
problems.statement: nums = [3, 1, 3, 2, 2, 4, 3, 1], k = 2, ties broken by smaller value.
problems.solution: 3 appears three times; 1 and 2 tie at two, and 1 is smaller, so the answer is [3, 1].

problems.title: heapify
problems.statement: Building a heap from n known items.
hints: Sift-down from the bottom: most nodes are near the leaves.
problems.solution: The sum over levels of (nodes × height) is O(n). Heapify-then-pop is O(n + k log n).

problems.title: C++ direction
hints: C++ defaults to a max-heap; Python to a min-heap.
problems.solution: Opposite defaults across languages are a classic source of bugs.

problems.title: Merge cost
problems.statement: Merging k = 1,000 sorted lists with N = 10⁶ elements in total, using a frontier heap.

parts.prompt: Heap operations, about N · log₂ k, in millions (log₂ 1000 ≈ 10)?

hints: One push and one pop per element.
problems.solution: N log k ≈ 10⁷; the heap never holds more than one element per list.

problems.title: Smallest pair sums
problems.statement: Find the k smallest a[i] + b[j] for sorted a and b.

parts.prompt: Pushing both (i + 1, j) and (i, j + 1) after each pop…
options: can push the same pair twice; use a visited set, or push (i + 1, j) only when j = 0

problems.solution: A frontier over an implicit sorted matrix. Avoid duplicates by construction or with a visited set.
